messages:
sam: Noticing a cluster oddity in us-west2 since ~04:05 UTC. Lots of GPU pods Pending but nodes report free GPUs.

maria: saw same. Scheduler logs: "no allocatable device: reservation mismatch" for pods that should fit.

yusuf: quick inspect shows nodes with taint gpu-ghost=true:NoSchedule and annotations like scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/gpu-reserve: token-zz9. Nodes still show .status.allocatable GPUs though.

sam: there's also a pattern of FailedAttachVolume events around the time the autoscaler trimmed warm nodes. Might be race where PVC detach didn't finish and leases remained.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled down nodepool-usw2-warm-gpu by 2 at 04:10 (utilization 0.09).

maria: workaround that worked for me: remove the taint and clear the stale annotation on affected nodes, then run a focused descheduler for pods annotated reservation=ghost. Example:

kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu-ghost=true:NoSchedule-
kubectl annotate node <node> scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/gpu-reserve-

whoever can, please coordinate rolling kubelet restarts on the 4 remaining flaky nodes to force lease reconciliation.

yusuf: I'll open a tracking ticket to add a guard into the autoscaler to avoid scaling down nodes with active GPU PVC/lease state and to add a descheduler rule for expired GPU reservations.

sam: thanks. let's capture dashboards and logs into the ticket and post a short blameless note to incidents.

ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-03-21-GPU-GHOST-LEASING
